record.original_question: Let L be a smooth differential operator that has been linearized in local charts to an n×n matrix, and write t_i = tr(L^i). Find an interpretation of the determinant identity det(L) = (1/n!) Σ_{π∈S_n} (−1)^{κ(π)-1} Z(π, t) as a genuine group-action or cycle-index formula, rather than only a symmetric-function proof.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 ... Then, we have det(L) = 1/n! Σ_{π∈S_n} (−1)^{κ(π)−1} Z(π, t). It's probably not hard to employ symmetric functions in proving (2). However, the above determinant behaves errily similar to a cycle index formula. So, find an interpretation of (2) as some appropriate group action.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be an $n\times n$ matrix over a field of characteristic $0$ (for example, the local matrix representation of a smooth linear operator in some chart), and for each positive integer $i$ set
$$t_i := \operatorname{tr}(L^i).$$
For a permutation $\pi\in S_n$ with cycle type $(c_1(\pi),c_2(\pi),\dots)$, where $c_k(\pi)$ is the number of $k$-cycles of $\pi$, write
$$Z(\pi,t):=\prod_{k\ge 1} t_k^{c_k(\pi)},$$
and let $\kappa(\pi)=\sum_k c_k(\pi)$ denote the total number of cycles of $\pi$. The classical Newton–Girard / Waring identity, equivalent to expressing the elementary symmetric polynomial $e_n$ in terms of the power sums $p_i$, gives
$$\det(L) \;=\; \frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}(-1)^{\kappa(\pi)-1}\,Z(\pi,t). \qquad (\ast)$$

The right-hand side of $(\ast)$ has the formal shape of a cycle index of the symmetric group $S_n$ acting on something, with the variables $x_k$ specialized to $t_k=\operatorname{tr}(L^k)$ and twisted by the sign $(-1)^{\kappa(\pi)-1}$.

Problem. Provide a genuine combinatorial / group-theoretic interpretation of the identity $(\ast)$: namely, exhibit an explicit action of $S_n$ (or of a suitable related group) on a set, vector space, or category naturally associated to $L$, together with a weighting/character of that action, such that summing the weight over orbits or averaging over the group recovers $\det(L)$ in the form $(\ast)$, thereby realizing $(\ast)$ as a bona fide cycle-index (Pólya-type) enumeration formula rather than merely an algebraic identity of symmetric functions.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for a Pólya-style cycle-index interpretation of the determinant formula expressing $\det(L)$ as a signed average over $S_n$ of the cycle-index monomials in the traces $\operatorname{tr}(L^k)$ returns only standard references on cycle indices of permutation groups (Wikipedia, MathWorld, Wolfram, expository notes) and no source providing a group-action interpretation of this specific signed identity. No paper or note resolving the problem could be located, so its current status is not determinable from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Cycle index - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A cycle index is a polynomial which encodes how a permutation group acts on a set; standard sources discuss only the unsigned Pólya cycle index.
status_evidence.claim: Standard literature defines cycle indices without sign-twists and does not address the signed determinant identity in question.

status_evidence.title: Cycle Index -- from Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: Z(X)=1/|X| sum_{alpha in X} prod_k x_k^{j_k(alpha)}.
status_evidence.claim: The classical cycle index has no sign factor, so an interpretation of the signed version is not provided by standard references.
